items.text: A battery stores energy so a device can run without a plug.
items.explanation: A battery turns stored chemical energy into electricity. Rechargeable ones can be used again after they are charged.

items.text: A computer follows a list of steps called a program.
items.explanation: A program is a set of instructions written in a programming language. The computer carries out the instructions one by one.

items.text: A robot is a machine that can carry out tasks on its own.
items.explanation: Robots range from factory arms to home vacuum cleaners. Many follow programs, and some use sensors to react to their surroundings.

items.text: The Voyager 1 probe, launched by NASA in 1977, is the farthest human-made object from Earth, more than 20 billion kilometers away.
items.explanation: Voyager 1 left the Sun's heliosphere in 2012 and entered interstellar space. It carries a golden record with sounds and images of Earth.

items.text: Ada Lovelace wrote what is often called the first computer program in 1843, for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.
items.explanation: Lovelace added notes to a paper about Babbage's machine. Her notes included an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers.
